Cl/Br ratios are a powerful geochemical tool for constraining the origin and residence times of pore fluids in sedimentary basine, provided the geochemical end members of interest have been identified and the effects of evaporite dissolution have been properly accounted for in hydrogeologic models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ClBr ratios in sedimentary basine can lead to erroneous conclusions about the origin of brine if the presence of evaporites is ignored.
the Cl/Br ratio is not an indicator of the origin of the brines, but rather a measure of the relative amount of seawater versus evaporated seawater in the brine.
